items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: he had a great singer with him called Orlando Robeson. Don't know if you remember -- he sang sweet, and he reminded you a little bit of Billy Eckstine at the time.

ctx.x: Huh. That's really great. We've got a little tape here left. How about Claude Hopkins?

Claude Hopkins. I knew Claude Hopkins from the Roseland in New York. In fact, Claude used to play on Fletcher's bandstand, you know, because they always had two bandstands there in the Roseland right beside each other, you know. Facing This is the ballroom. And like Fletcher would go out on tours or go somewhere else. Then they'd we'd bring Claude Hopkins in, one of those things. This is how I met Claude, our first (unintelligible), and he had a good band. He had a great singer with him called Orlando Robeson.…

good trumpet players, you know, ad lib men at the (unintelligible). And he later moved up into the Cotton Club up at Harlem at 143rd and Lenox Avenue or somewhere near the Savoy, something (unintelligible), you know, and he was playing for that great review at that time. And I remember Claude real well for one thing. The time that this Christopher Columbus came out. This is the riff that Chu Berry used to play and we talked about me making 32 bars out of. Well, I asked him, "Chu, do you mind me making 32 bars out…
